title: Test my MCP server
subtitle: Heimdall checks how your MCP server behaves, then standard agents use it on real tasks. The report shows which tools help agents and which mislead them.

form.heading: Your server
form.urlHint: The streamable HTTP endpoint of your server.
form.inspectNote: Free: no model is used. Sends a small batch of requests, including some deliberately malformed ones, and takes under a minute.
form.secretHint: An org secret. Add one under Settings, Secrets.
form.callReadOnly: Call tools the server marks read-only, with sample inputs
form.callReadOnlyHint: Other tools are never called. Without this, only the deliberate bad requests run.

result.unstable: The tool list changed between two requests in one session.
result.scanNone: No hidden instructions or tool poisoning found in what the server shows an agent.

draft.heading: Benchmark your server with standard agents
draft.hint: One task per tool. Agents such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode run each task against your live server, and every call is recorded. The tasks start as drafts for you to review.
draft.failed: The benchmark could not be created.
draft.noReference: {{n}} tasks have no proven reference yet (their tool was not called during the check). Put inputs your server accepts into their reference before the readiness check: {{ids}}.
draft.noKeyedAgent: None of the reference agents (claude-code, codex, opencode) has a model key in this organization. Add an OpenAI or Anthropic key first.
draft.next: Next: run the readiness check on the benchmark page, review each task, then evaluate.
